chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from 'Isa said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man upon whom the prayer of a year due to illness has accumulated, he said, 'He does not make it up.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'This report is interpreted as referring to the voluntary prayers; what indicates this is what he narrated:'

key_terms.صَلاَةُ سَنَةٍ: Prayer of a year (accumulated missed prayers)
key_terms.لاَ يَقْضِي: He does not make it up (no qada required)

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to make up missed prayers if they were ill for a long time?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that a person who missed prayers for a year due to illness does not need to make them up (*qada*). Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentary clarifies that this ruling specifically applies to voluntary (*nawafil*) prayers, distinguishing them from obligatory (*fard*) prayers which typically require makeup, thereby highlighting the jurisprudential nuance between the two categories in cases of prolonged incapacity.
